This template's method is the opposite of every other one in the bank: it barely argues with the camera at all, and buys its realism by committing to particulars - a clock time, named brands, six objects in the background, a mark on the bridge of the nose from a pair of sunglasses. Nothing here is a quality word. Every slot is a decision that could have gone another way, and that is precisely why the result reads as a photograph of one real morning rather than a rendering of a type of person.
inventory-selfie.source_note: Reverse-engineered from a fifth community-supplied image prompt contributed by the user - a Reformer Pilates changing-room mirror selfie. NOT AI Video Bootcamp course material. Kept as its own template rather than folded into the influencer series because the method is genuinely different and in one respect opposite: that template fixes a look so it can be repeated, while this one spends everything on detail that could only be true once, and it has no lock at all. It is also the only template in this bank where the phone is IN the picture rather than being the camera - the exact inverse of the selfie-monologue video template's ownership lock, and worth reading next to it. Nothing was dropped from the source; the brand names were kept, with the `jewellery` slot's `why` explaining what they are actually buying and where they stop working.

slots.label: Frame and hour
slots.does: The kind of photograph, who is in it, where, and what time it is.
slots.why: The clock time is the most undervalued clause in the whole prompt. It is not a lighting instruction - the light gets named later - it is a commitment, and it decides things the prompt never says: how full the room is, what state she is in, what has already happened that day. A mid-morning weekday changing room is nearly empty and everyone in it has finished a class. 'Daytime' buys none of that.
slots.example: Ultra-realistic photorealistic full-length mirror selfie, true-to-life, of a 26-year-old blonde woman in the changing-room corridor of a Reformer Pilates studio at 11:05am on an ordinary weekday morning, candid, phone angled down at the mirror at eye level

slots.label: Hair
slots.does: How it is worn, and the thing holding it.
slots.why: Worth a slot of its own because it carries the hour: hair slicked back and tied is hair that has just been worked in, and it reads that way without the prompt ever saying she exercised. Naming what holds it - a specific scrunchie rather than 'a hair tie' - is the same trick as the jewellery slot below, one object standing in for a whole level of care.
slots.example: hair slicked back into a low ponytail held with a black silk scrunchie, a few flyaway strands escaping at the temples

slots.label: Jewellery
slots.does: The small metal, named piece by piece.
slots.why: A named piece has a shape the model already knows: a huggie, a paperclip chain and a hinged bangle are three specific silhouettes, where 'gold jewellery' is none. Brand names work as shorthand for those silhouettes plus a price bracket, and that is all they are buying - so lean on them for the shape and expect nothing more. Where they stop working is logos: ask for a brand whose mark is its identity and the model will try to render the mark, badly. If the piece is only recognisable by its logo, describe the object instead.
slots.example: a single small gold huggie in each ear, a slim gold paperclip necklace, a hinged love bracelet in yellow gold on one wrist, a thin gold anklet

slots.label: Wardrobe
slots.does: Every garment, with its colour, finish and how it is being worn right now.
slots.why: The finish is what stops this reading as a catalogue: matte black photographs nothing like the same black in a technical knit, and 'half-unzipped' is a state rather than a garment, which is what makes it look like something she is wearing rather than something she is modelling. Bone-white socks with white trainers is the level of specificity this template runs at - two whites that are not the same white.
slots.example: wearing a matte-black cropped long-sleeve zip-up, half-unzipped over a white ribbed bra, matching high-waisted black leggings, white suede trainers with bone-white socks

slots.label: What she is holding
slots.does: The objects in her hands and on her shoulder, including the phone taking the picture.
slots.why: Hands with something in them are hands that behave. This is also the one template where the phone is deliberately IN frame and held at a stated angle - the exact opposite of the selfie-monologue video template, where the whole clip depends on the device never appearing. Naming the cup, the straw and the bag is what fills the second hand and stops it drifting into the generic open palm a model reaches for when a hand has no job.
slots.example: holding an iced oat-milk matcha in a hard plastic reusable cup with a pink silicone straw, a tan leather bucket bag slung on one shoulder, the phone in the other hand angled down at the mirror

slots.label: Pose and eyeline
slots.does: What her body is doing, her expression, and where she is actually looking.
slots.why: The eyeline is the slot. In a mirror selfie she is looking at her screen, not at herself and not at the lens - and that small wrongness is what makes the photograph read as taken rather than posed for. A closed-mouth smile is the other half: it is what a face does when it is checking a frame, not performing for one.
slots.example: head tilted slightly, weight settled on one hip, a small closed-mouth smile, unposed, her eyes on the phone screen rather than her own reflection

slots.label: Evidence of a life
slots.does: The marks a body carries from things that happened before the photograph.
slots.why: The best idea in this prompt, and the one no generator adds unasked. A faint dent on the bridge of the nose means she wore sunglasses here; a tan line at the shoulder means a swimsuit, somewhere else, weeks ago; a small tattoo on the inner wrist means a decision. None of these describe how she looks - they are evidence, and evidence is what a photograph has and a rendering does not. This is the same instinct as asking for flyaway hairs, one level deeper: not imperfection for its own sake, but imperfection with a cause.
slots.example: a small geometric tattoo on the inner wrist, a faint mark on the bridge of the nose where sunglasses sat earlier, a barely-there tan line from a swimsuit strap at the shoulder

slots.label: Background inventory
slots.does: Everything visible in the mirror behind her, counted out - including another person who is not the subject.
slots.why: Six named objects instead of one named place. 'A Pilates changing room' returns a stock interior; lockers with brass fobs, rolled towels, a reed diffuser and a eucalyptus wreath return a room somebody works in. The second woman, out of focus and doing something unrelated, is the single strongest clause here - a room with one person in it is a set, and a room with somebody incidentally tying a shoelace is a place. Note also the small pink sign reading one word: this is the one time these prompts ask for rendered TEXT, and it works precisely because it is a short word, in a known object, at a small size - which is the same conclusion tools/typography_bank.json reaches from the other direction with its `whisper` ratio.
slots.example: behind her in the mirror: a row of small wooden lockers with brass key-fobs, a shelf of rolled white towels, a reed diffuser on a low cabinet, a soft-pink sign reading 'breathe', a eucalyptus wreath on a door, and another woman out of focus tying her shoelaces on a bench

slots.label: Capture
slots.does: The device, and the honest artefacts of shooting a mirror with it.
slots.why: The fingerprint smear on the mirror edge is the detail to copy out of this prompt. It is not about the subject at all - it is about the surface between the camera and the subject, and a smudge on glass is something no one would invent and everyone's mirror has. Naming the device without naming its flaws gets you a clean render of a phone photograph; naming one flaw gets you a phone photograph.
slots.example: shot on an iPhone 15 Pro front camera, no flash, a slight fingerprint smear on the mirror edge catching the light, very mild HDR holding the dynamic range, not overly polished

slots.label: Lens
slots.does: The focal length, and how much of the room behind her stays sharp.
slots.why: A front camera is wide, and wide is why a mirror selfie looks like a mirror selfie: the corridor stretches away behind her and her nearer hand reads slightly larger. Saying so stops the model delivering a flattering portrait-length rendering of a scene that a phone would have shown much wider.
slots.example: 24mm-wide front camera perspective, deep enough depth of field to keep the lockers legible while the woman further down the bench falls gently out of focus

slots.label: Light
slots.does: The building's own light, named as the fittings that make it.
slots.why: Warm LED cove lighting is a specific, unglamorous, entirely real way a room like this is lit - hidden strips bouncing off a ceiling, no visible source, nothing dramatic. It is worth naming exactly because it is not a photographer's setup: the whole premise is that nobody lit this, and 'soft warm light' would invite the model to light it anyway.
slots.example: soft warm LED cove lighting bounced off the ceiling with no visible source and no flash, gentle realistic shadows under the shelf, even daylight-neutral fill along the corridor

slots.label: Skin
slots.does: Skin twenty minutes after exercise, described as what it is doing rather than how good it looks.
slots.why: 'Post-workout glow' is doing real work: it names a state - warm, slightly damp, flushed unevenly - where 'glowing skin' names a wish. Pairing it with visible pores and no makeup beyond a balm is what keeps a model from resolving the glow into a sheen it airbrushes everything else to match.
slots.example: clean post-workout skin, faintly damp at the hairline, an uneven pink flush across the cheekbones, visible pores across the nose, real tonal variation, no makeup beyond a tinted lip balm and a brow gel

slots.label: Grade
slots.does: The colour treatment, in the vocabulary of a phone rather than a film.
slots.why: Last, and deliberately restrained. Everything above has been specific, so the grade's job is only to not undo it: warm highlights, soft falloff, mild processing. A strong grade on a prompt this detailed flattens the forty decisions above into a look, which is the one way this method can still fail.
slots.example: warm oat-and-cream highlights, soft shadow falloff, realistic contrast, natural skin tones, clean modern editorial colour grading with nothing pushed
